🎋 When to plant sugarcane in Nigeria

Also called Ìrèké (Yoruba) and Rake (Hausa).

Quick answer: Plant sugarcane in Nigeria from March to May and November to December and harvest from November to April. Setts are planted with the rains or under irrigation; cane is harvested in the dry season.

PlantMarch to May and November to December
HarvestNovember to April
Grows inNorth-Central, North-West, North-East and South-West
TypeTree & cash crops
Local namesÌrèké · Rake

About sugarcane

Large sugar estates include Bacita (Kwara) and Savannah Sugar at Numan (Adamawa).

How to plant sugarcane well

Plant healthy setts with 2–3 buds each.

Setts are planted with the rains or under irrigation; cane is harvested in the dry season.

Diseases and pests of sugarcane

  • Sugarcane smutPlant resistant varieties and healthy setts.
  • Red rotAvoid infected setts and waterlogged fields.

Best states for sugarcane

Kwara · Niger · Kano · Kaduna · Jigawa · Adamawa · Taraba · Kebbi

Questions farmers ask

When is the best time to plant sugarcane in Nigeria?

Plant sugarcane in Nigeria from March to May and November to December and harvest from November to April. Setts are planted with the rains or under irrigation; cane is harvested in the dry season.

What is sugarcane called in Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo?

Sugarcane is called Ìrèké (Yoruba) and Rake (Hausa).

When is sugarcane harvested in Nigeria?

Sugarcane is usually harvested from November to April.

Which Nigerian states grow the most sugarcane?

Kwara, Niger, Kano, Kaduna, Jigawa, Adamawa, Taraba and Kebbi are among the best-known sugarcane states.

Can I grow sugarcane in my part of Nigeria?

Sugarcane grows best in the North-Central, North-West, North-East and South-West regions. In other regions, ask your ADP extension officer before planting.

What diseases attack sugarcane and how do I prevent them?

Sugarcane smut: Plant resistant varieties and healthy setts. Red rot: Avoid infected setts and waterlogged fields.
